writerNotes: piece: the hero tattoos one design on a forearm. Pick the drawn design that suits the studio (swallow, rose, dagger, moth or heart), bold for traditional work or fine for fine line, three inks (main colour, the banner, then leaves, wings or the blade), an optional short word on a banner (or empty), a skin tone, and the caption on the healed photo. Write the six stages for that piece in the studio's voice.
count: hours the piece takes, needles and inks used and how long it heals, kept modest and honest. session.start is when the sitting begins; session.clock is 12h in the US, otherwise 24h.

flash: four to eight designs from the brief, each drawn as the nearest of the five designs with three inks and an optional banner word; mark taken ones claimed. If the brief has no flash, make a plain set in the studio's style with prices that fit its rates.
book: sizes with realistic hours, places with how much slower than a forearm they are (ribs and hands are slower), the brief's artists, and its rates exactly. The form is a demo: nothing is sent.
care: standard, safe aftercare unless the brief gives its own; never medical claims.

hero.title and hero.titleEm: a short two-part headline (four lines at most on a desktop); section titles have a second half. theme.accent is the studio's colour, deep enough for white button text; theme.wordmarkFit is always "fit".
business.name is set to exactly the name in the brief and cannot be changed; brand.name is how it appears in the nav and the footer (short).
